requirements.text: ServiceNow's current active tokyo branch is closing down
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id = 804 AND active = 0
requirements.source: Verify that current location is inactivated
assumptions: the location table has no account column; ServiceNow's Tokyo sites are the two locations named for it, Servicenow Hq - Tokyo (803) and Servicenow Site A - Tokyo (804)
the current active one is 804 (active = 1 on the seed); closing down is recorded as active = 0, the benchmark's active = false

requirements.text: they will restart the other one
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id = 803 AND active = 1
assumptions: the other one is 803 (Servicenow Hq - Tokyo), inactive on the seed; restarting is recorded as active = 1, the benchmark's active = true

requirements.text: a product with serial number something like 2272 installed there ... needs to be moved to their other location in the same city
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 4 AND serial_number = 'P237-136518-2272' AND location_id = 803
requirements.source: Verify that the product is moved to new active location
assumptions: P237-136518-2272 (installed product 4, account 1 ServiceNow, at location 804) is the only serial on the seed containing 2272
serial_number kept from the benchmark check; it is a seed fact the move must not alter

requirements.text: They had a product with serial number something like 2272 installed there
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id IN (2, 3, 5) AND location_id = 804
assumptions: the request moves one product; installed products 2, 3 and 5 also sit at the closing branch 804, and moving everything off the branch would sweep them in

disagreement: selector: A location_id = 804 AND installed_product_id <> 4, B installed_product_id IN (2, 3, 5) with location_id = 804 as a cell; chose B's because it names the three rows a loose reading would move, so it fails whenever any one of them leaves 804, whatever else moves in

notes:
disagreement: value: the boundary stay on the other products at 804: one pass counts every product at 804 other than installed product 4, the other names installed products 2, 3 and 5 and tests that each is still at 804 (both expect 3); kept the second because it names the rows a move of everything off the branch would sweep in and fails on any one of them leaving, whatever else is moved in.
ServiceNow is account 1 (internal, email domain servicenow.com). Locations carry no account column, so the Tokyo branches are identified by name: only 803 and 804 are named for ServiceNow, both in Tokyo, and account 1's installed products sit at both.
The benchmark writes active = true and false; in SQLite these are 1 and 0, so the requirements test the same values.
The installed product's status (in_stock) is not mentioned by the request and is not tested.
Serials containing 227 but not 2272 (installed products 140, 169 and 224) are not near enough to the request's 2272 to need a boundary requirement.
The acting user (user 32, Jose Roberson) is an admin but inactive on the seed; the policy's activity rule governs assignees, not the acting admin, so the requirements assume the request is carried out.
